# Squint

> Squint (https://squint.mdzabeeh.com) is a free, browser-based arcade of
> five-minute games that train a designer's instincts: visual accuracy,
> letter spacing (kerning), colour perception and divergent thinking.
> Tagline: "Train the eye you trust." No account needed; camera-based games
> run entirely on-device and never upload video.

## Games

- [Eyeball It](https://squint.mdzabeeh.com/eyeball-it/): bisect, centre,
  judge angles and proportions by eye; scored on pixel error with
  design-spec redline feedback and micro-lessons (e.g. optical vs
  geometric centre).
- [Kern Combat](https://squint.mdzabeeh.com/kern-combat/): drag letters to
  even spacing, graded against the typeface's own kerning metrics; teaches
  the optical rules of letter spacing.
- [Colour Forge](https://squint.mdzabeeh.com/colour-forge/): mix HSL colour
  to match targets (including from memory and by complement); scored with
  the perceptual CIEDE2000 formula plus a per-channel breakdown.
- [Cutout](https://squint.mdzabeeh.com/cutout/): two overlapping shapes are
  shown next to the silhouette that one boolean operation produced, and you
  name the operation: union, intersect, exclude, or either subtraction.
  Order is treated as part of the answer, since A minus B is a different
  shape from B minus A. Trains the mental model behind Figma's boolean
  operations and Illustrator's Pathfinder.
- [Steady Hand](https://squint.mdzabeeh.com/steady-hand/): trace a Bézier
  curve in a single stroke, starting from a marker. Deviation from the path
  and how much of it you covered are scored separately, and the reveal
  distinguishes drifting off a consistent line from an unsteady one. Curve
  types cover arcs, S-curves, tight radii, long sweeps, hooks and waves.
- [Contrast Call](https://squint.mdzabeeh.com/contrast-call/): read a colour
  pair shown as real text and call its WCAG contrast ratio on a logarithmic
  rail from 1:1 to 21:1, with the 3:1, 4.5:1 and 7:1 thresholds marked; the
  true ratio and its AA/AAA verdict are then revealed. Rounds rotate through
  greyscale, warm and cool hues, clashing opposites, pairs straddling 4.5:1,
  and the compressed ends of the scale.
- [Double Take](https://squint.mdzabeeh.com/double-take/): two renderings of
  one real interface card (a profile, a product listing, a player, a metric
  tile, a notification) sit side by side and exactly one carries a single
  deliberate flaw: broken alignment, an uneven gap, a weak size step, text
  under 4.5:1 contrast, a mismatched corner radius, lopsided padding, an
  off-centre icon, a mis-grouped label or an odd-sized sibling icon. Pick
  the clean one; the flaw is then named and measured with the principle
  behind it. Flaws get subtler as the session progresses.
- [Thirty Circles](https://squint.mdzabeeh.com/thirty-circles/): the classic
  Bob McKim / IDEO divergent-thinking sprint: thirty circles into thirty
  different things in three minutes; drawn by webcam-tracked hand or mouse;
  reflection on fluency, flexibility, originality.
- [Hand Tetris](https://squint.mdzabeeh.com/tetris/): gesture-controlled
  Tetris via on-device MediaPipe hand tracking.
- [Daily Warm-Up](https://squint.mdzabeeh.com/warm-up/): one round each of
  four games sampled fresh daily, chained into a five-minute ritual with
  streak tracking.

## How it teaches

Every round ends with a teach-back reveal (the correct answer overlaid on
the player's attempt, the error measured, and the design principle behind
the miss), progress is tracked locally with accuracy trends, and round
selection adapts toward the player's weakest challenge types.

## More

- [About & FAQ](https://squint.mdzabeeh.com/about/): what Squint is, who
  it's for, privacy details, and how scoring works.
- [Focalism](https://squint.mdzabeeh.com/focalism/): the design language
  invented for Squint, "hierarchy is focus": depth via focal planes
  instead of shadows, focus-rack transitions, signal-only colour, and
  chromatic aberration marking errors. Manifesto, live specimens and
  CSS adoption recipes. Squint is the reference implementation.
